affordance_in_statement: To ensure every workstation is active around the clock, its two trained workers must be distributed across the two shifts: one must be assigned to shift 1, and the other to shift 2.
removal_suggestion: No semantics-preserving removal is available: assigning one endpoint of every pair to each of two shifts is exactly a bipartite 2-coloring constraint. Rewording it would only disguise, not remove, the core task.

common_affordance: Each workstation imposes an opposite-shift constraint on its two workers, which is intrinsically equivalent to bipartite graph coloring.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It incorrectly treats odd vertex degree as evidence of impossibility, apparently confusing bipartiteness with an even-degree condition. A valid bipartite path can contain vertices of odd degree.

recommended_edit: No valid single edit can defeat all surviving models without changing the problem's core semantics; the survivors are solving the required bipartite-coloring problem directly.
